fieldValues.title: extension-dependency work is RFC-042 Revision 4, not a standalone RFC-043
fieldValues.summary: srs#565's remaining scope (extensions regrouped by dependency, a stated adds/depends/cost shape) is normatively defined in rfcs/rfc-042-concept-tree-spine.md's Revision 4 (Change I, Conformance Rules [R14]-[R19]) -- not in a separate rfc-043-*.md file. A next unit reading srs#565 or looking for "RFC-043" should look at RFC-042 Revision 4 instead; the RFC number was never assigned because the content amends RFC-042's own [R2]/[R4] surface (Door 3), not new normative meaning under a fresh RFC number (Door 2). PR: srs#783. Tracking issue srs#782 was originally filed and titled as a standalone RFC-043 before this reclassification; its title and body now point at RFC-042 Revision 4.
fieldValues.rationale: A standalone RFC-043 draft passed a two-reviewer Stage 3 pass with a blocking finding: it amended RFC-042's own [R2] ('a leaf has exactly one parent, which is a concept') and [R4] ('a leaf never carries a depends-on edge') directly, which CLAUDE.md's own Door taxonomy calls Door 3 ('amends an accepted RFC's own surface... an RFC revision... in the SAME PR'), not Door 2 ('new normative meaning... an RFC'). The RFC-041 Revision 4 precedent (a Door-3 fold folded into the existing RFC's own file rather than filed separately) was followed instead of minting RFC-043. Reopens only if a future change to this same territory turns out to need genuinely new normative meaning unrelated to RFC-042's existing [R2]/[R4] -- at that point a fresh RFC number is the right call again, not a further RFC-042 revision.
